title: Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy
provenance: reported by HappySmurfday (highball#63) on an Epic copy; reproduced here on the Steam copy, M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r4, 2026-09-09
notes: DirectX 12 only: on DXMT it stops at "No suitable D3D12 adapter found" before the splash, confirmed here 2026-09-09, so D3DMetal is the only mode that can reach the game and this row exists to make Highball ask for Apple's licence at the first launch. Under D3DMetal the splash and its menu render correctly, then the game crashes on Play Game. The crash is NOT the DirectX 12 timestamp problem this entry used to claim: reproduced here with Highball's timestamp shim loaded and active (both the shim's d3d12 and Apple's library behind it appear in the crash dump's module list) and the crash is byte for byte identical. It is an unhandled page fault reading 0x907, and disassembling the engine's kernelbase places the faulting instruction 0x44 bytes inside SwitchToFiber, reading offset 8 of the fiber pointer it was given. The register dump shows that pointer as 0x8ff, a small integer rather than an address, so the game hands Wine an invalid fiber and Wine dereferences it. The game imports CreateFiber, DeleteFiber, FlsAlloc and IsThreadAFiber for its job system. Where the bad value comes from is not established.

requiresLauncher.name: Epic Games Launcher
requiresLauncher.note: Reported with the Epic copy; the Steam copy has not been tried.

knownIssues.symptom: Crashes on "Play Game" from the splash screen, with Wine's "has encountered a serious problem" dialog, on D3DMetal. The AVX toggle makes no difference.
knownIssues.cause: an invalid fiber pointer, not a graphics fault. Reproduced 2026-09-09 on an M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-crossover26.3-r4, Steam copy: unhandled page fault on read of 0x907, faulting instruction 0x44 bytes into SwitchToFiber (confirmed by disassembling the engine's kernelbase, not by guessing the nearest symbol), reading offset 8 of the fiber pointer in rcx, which the register dump shows as 0x8ff. The backtrace is three frames of game code straight into kernelbase with no graphics library between. The previous entry blamed D3DMetal's missing DirectX 12 timestamp queries and named Highball's shim as the fix; that is retracted. The shim was loaded and active during this reproduction and changed nothing, because timestamps were never the cause.
knownIssues.fix: none known. Highball's timestamp shim does NOT fix this game, contrary to what this entry said between 0.8.7 and 2026-09-09. The shim remains correct for what it was built for, D3DMetal reporting a timestamp frequency of 60 and resolving timestamp queries to zero, which is still true and still measurable with a probe. It is simply not what stops Guardians.
